english.notes:
(i) Proceedings for an offence under this Act may be brought within the period of 6 months beginning with the date on which evidence sufficient in the opinion of the prosecutor to warrant the proceedings came to his knowledge (section 9(3)), but subsection (3) does not authorise the commencement of proceedings for an offence more than 2 years after the date on which the offence was committed (section 9(4) Deer Act 1991).
(ii) A certificate signed by the or on behalf of the prosecutor and stating the date on which evidence sufficient in his opinion to warrant the proceedings came to his knowledge shall be conclusive evidence of that fact (section 9(5)). A certificate stating that matter and purporting to be so signed shall be deemed to be so signed unless the contrary is proved (section 9(6)).
(iii) Section 12(1) of the Deer Act 1991 provides that If a constable suspects with reasonable cause that any person is committing or has committed an offence under the Act, the constable may without warrant-
(a) stop and search that person if the constable suspects without reasonable cause that evidence of the commission of the offence is to be found on that person;
(b) search or examine any vehicle, animal, weapon or other thing which that person may then be using if the constable suspects with reasonable cause that evidence of the commission of the offence is to be found on that vehicle, animal, weapon or other thing;
(c) seize and detain for the purposes of proceedings under this Act anything which is evidence of the commission of the offence and any deer, venison, vehicle, animal, weapon or other thing which is liable to be forfeited under section 13.
(iv Section 12(2) of the Deer Act 1991 provides that for the purposes of-
(a) exercising the powers conferred under subsection (1) above, or
(b) arresting a person, in accordance with section 24 of the Police and Criminal Evidence Act 1984 (arrest conditions), for an offence under this Act, a constable may enter any land other than a dwelling-house.
(v) Section 12(3) of the Deer Act 1991 provides that a constable may sell any deer or venison seized under this section and the net proceeds of the sale shall be liable to be detained and forfeited in the same manner as the deer or venison sold; but he shall not be subject to any liability on account of his neglect or failure to exercise the powers conferred on him by this subsection.
(vi) Section 13(1) of the Deer Act 1991 provides that the court by which a person is convicted of any offence under this Act may order the forfeiture of-
(a) any deer or venison in respect of which the offence was committed or which was found in that person's possession;
(b) any vehicle, animal, weapon or other thing which was used to commit the offence or which was capable of being used to take, kill, or injure deer and was found in his possession.
(vii) Section 13(2) of the Deer Act 1991 provides that where the offence of which the person is convicted is an offence under section 1, the court (without prejudice to its powers under subsection (1) above) may cancel any firearm or shotgun certificate held by him.
